macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks finish slightly lower as chip weakness offsets bank earnings
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.35% to 51,670.10, the S&P 500 slipped 0.02% to 7,805.45, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.15% to 27,204.38. Semiconductor stocks remained under pressure, while investors gave a mixed reception to major-bank results.[5]

items.title: Markets await September CPI for clues on Fed policy
items.summary: Investors are focused on Wednesday’s U.S. September consumer-price report, which could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve’s next policy move. Futures markets were pricing a 78% chance of no change at the Fed’s upcoming meeting and roughly a 70% probability of a December rate hike.[7]

items.title: New York Fed’s Williams still sees one 2026 rate hike, no 2027 increase for now
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said another rate increase could be appropriate this year but that he currently sees no need for further tightening in 2027. He cited continued disinflation and limited broad price pressure outside areas such as artificial intelligence and energy.[9]

items.title: Bank earnings draw mixed investor reaction
items.summary: JPMorgan, Citigroup and Wells Fargo reported quarterly results, but market reactions were negative or muted: Citigroup dropped 5.6%, Wells Fargo fell 3.1%, and JPMorgan declined 0.9%. JPMorgan reported earnings and revenue below analyst expectations, while Wells Fargo missed on net interest income.[1]

items.title: Bumble to be taken private in $1.3 billion deal
items.summary: Bumble shares surged 56.6% after Ithaca Holdings announced an all-cash agreement to acquire the dating-app company in a transaction valued at approximately $1.3 billion.[7]

items.title: Asian markets rise as traders assess Fed and Bank of Japan signals
items.summary: Asian equities gained after Williams indicated that additional Fed tightening beyond a possible 2026 hike may not be needed. Bank of Japan officials were reportedly leaning against another immediate rate increase while keeping open the possibility of a move in December.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds toward $83,000 as crypto market stabilizes
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered from an intraday decline near $81,000 to around $83,500, while Ethereum traded near $2,508. The broader market was supported by easing concern over additional Federal Reserve tightening.[9]

items.title: More than $727 million in crypto positions liquidated
items.summary: About 156,000 traders were liquidated over 24 hours, totaling roughly $727.5 million, while spot Bitcoin and Ethereum exchange-traded funds recorded net outflows of $65.4 million and $85.4 million, respectively.[10]

items.title: Blockchain.com seeks U.S. licenses for prediction markets and derivatives
items.summary: Blockchain.com reportedly applied for Commodity Futures Trading Commission licenses that would allow it to offer event contracts and crypto derivatives to U.S. customers. The move comes as the company prepares for a potential public listing.[3]

items.title: CFTC outlines crypto framework focused on investor protection
items.summary: CFTC Chair Mike Selig said the agency’s proposed framework is intended to create federal oversight protecting exchange customers from fraud, market manipulation and misuse of customer funds, with the FTX collapse cited as a key concern.[5]

items.title: Strive expands Bitcoin holdings through equity financing
items.summary: Strive increased its Bitcoin holdings by 11% through warrant activity, making it the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, according to reported market coverage.[1]

items.title: Tron activates post-quantum cryptography on testnet
items.summary: Tron announced that it activated post-quantum cryptography on its testnet and said the upgrade could proceed to mainnet after testing.[1]

items.title: NEAR outperforms amid broader crypto sell-off
items.summary: NEAR reportedly held up better than the broader market as an artificial-intelligence investment narrative supported the token, while Bitcoin fell about 3.2% and Ethereum declined about 7% in the cited session.[4]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon AI model
items.summary: Google released its flagship Gemini 4 Argon model globally to developers, businesses and Gemini users, positioning it as a larger, more capable model for cybersecurity, engineering and enterprise workflows. The model is being offered through Google’s paid API and cloud platforms, with introductory pricing reported at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

items.title: Meta unveils Muse Wonder and Wonder Full models
items.summary: Meta introduced two frontier AI models, Muse Wonder and the higher-performance Wonder Full, emphasizing long-running agentic tasks, coding, multi-step reasoning and persistent conversational memory. The models are expected to be integrated into Meta’s Muse assistant, initially for paid subscribers.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Epic delays Disney collaboration amid major AI pivot
items.summary: Epic Games reportedly postponed an upcoming shooter featuring Marvel and Star Wars characters, while directing developers to adopt an “AI-first” production process. CEO Tim Sweeney separately confirmed a broad shift toward accelerating development with artificial intelligence.

items.title: Microsoft launches Xbox Labs
items.summary: Microsoft is establishing Xbox Labs, an initiative focused on emerging technologies, cross-platform development, AI, and experiments involving game decompilation and recompilation.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day reportedly launches on Xbox and PC
items.summary: Microsoft announced the full release of The Coalition’s Gears of War: E-Day on Xbox Series X|S and PC, including availability through Xbox Game Pass Ultimate. The title was also reportedly targeted by a distributed-denial-of-service attack.

items.title: God of War: Laufey collector’s edition criticized for excluding the game
items.summary: A newly announced collector’s edition for God of War: Laufey has drawn criticism because the package includes collectibles but requires buyers to purchase the base game separately.

items.title: U.S. video-game spending fell 9% in August
items.summary: Circana data reported a 9% year-over-year decline in U.S. video-game spending for August. NBA 2K27 led full-game dollar sales, while several new releases entered the month’s top 10.
